shared_elements: quadruped animals in strict profile, carved in low relief
horizontal band of repeated linear motifs
animals with elongated bodies and prominent heads/snouts
flat, undecorated background around raised figures
rough-hewn rectangular stone block/slab as the carrying surface
justification: Both surfaces present processions of profile quadrupeds in shallow raised relief, stacked in horizontal registers on a plain field of coarse pale stone, with a strip of repeated linear/geometric motifs acting as a divider and a snouted animal head at the lower edge — a fairly specific compositional scheme. The biggest difference is the format and density: A is a single low rectangular block whose whole face is filled with an overlapping tangle of similar quadrupeds, while B is a tall stepped pillar with clearly separated registers containing a wider variety of subjects (birds, a long-necked bird, a snake-like form) and much more empty ground between them.
